Field notes · No. 1

Start with the tab you can’t close

DJ, founderJuly 28, 20262 min read

Every app wants you to start with a template. I’d rather you start with the tab you can’t close.

Mine, last spring, was StreetEasy. Fourteen listings across three browser windows, and a screenshot of a floor plan I’d zoomed into so many times the pixels had opinions. Also a Notes file called “apts FINAL final.” I was leaving a fourth-floor walk-up in the East Village for somewhere in Brooklyn with a window that faced something other than a wall.

So that’s where my first board came from. Not a “life OS.” One board, called Moving.

Here’s the whole method. It takes about ten minutes.

  1. Paste what’s already open. Don’t organize first. I pasted the three listings I actually cared about. Each one became a card with its photo, and the other eleven tabs stopped mattering.
  2. Draw one region around the ones that are real. Mine said “Under $3,200, near the G.” If you know the G, you know that’s a commitment.
  3. Write down the thing you keep saying out loud. “The fridge gap is 62 cm.” I’d said it to my partner three times. Once it was on the board, I didn’t have to say it again.
  4. Move one card to Done today. Booking Saturday’s viewing took thirty seconds. Dragging that card into Done is when the board started to feel like mine.

That’s it. No tags, no system. A week later it had grown a floor plan, and an arrow from the fridge note to the place in Greenpoint that was going to win. It won.

What surprised me came after. When the move was done, I didn’t archive anything. The board is a folder of plain files in my Dropbox, sitting next to the lease. Some nights I open it the way you’d flip through an old notebook.

I built Nook for the few things that are actually happening: a move, a trip, a thesis chapter, a book that won’t leave you alone. Each one gets a quiet corner. Your inbox and your to-do app can keep the rest.

So what’s the tab you can’t close right now? Make that your first board. Call it what you’d call it out loud. Paste three things, and move one to Done before bed.
